findings.claim: Paragraph 4 states a blanket cast-box result and then contradicts it two clauses later without any exception marker, and the Q3 rationale silently repairs the contradiction with a qualifier that is not in the passage.
findings.evidence: Passage: "The cast boxes held to three degrees or less, and two were used. Both of those two sat on a chimney breast whose flue still carried warm air up from the block's boiler, and the loggers inside them recorded a swing much like the timber's" — and "The timber boxes moved about eleven degrees between afternoon and dawn". Read literally, all twelve cast boxes held to <=3 degrees, yet two of those same twelve recorded ~11 degrees. The Q3 rationale reconciles this by writing "Cast material by itself held three degrees or less"; the words "by itself" appear nowhere in the passage, which says only "The cast boxes held to three degrees or less".
findings.why: Numbers that will not reconcile inside one paragraph are explicitly in the integrated stage's charter. It is scored minor, not major, because the intended reading (general result stated first, external-heat exception explained immediately after) is recoverable and Q3's key A remains the single best answer — the same sentence pair independently grants the two boxes a timber-like swing, so no distractor becomes defensible and no key moves. A one-word repair in the passage (e.g. "The cast boxes held to three degrees or less, with two exceptions") would remove the tension and let the rationale drop its unsupported gloss.

findings.claim: The trap label on Q2 option C names a trap type that is not the trap actually operating.
findings.evidence: Q2 rationale: "C = quantifier_upgrade / contradicted — turns the void into a single fixed spot and denies the movement the loggers recorded". Option C reads "They were narrow enough that a colony had to settle near the ridge and stay there for the whole season." No quantifier from the passage is absolutised in C; the passage's own words are "A void of that kind is not one habitat but a shifting range of them", which C denies outright. The mechanism is contradiction / scope collapse, not quantifier upgrade. Contrast Q1/A, where the label is exact: the planted hedge "fills most summers" really is absolutised into "occupied every single summer".
findings.why: "Trap labels name the actual trap" is an integrated-stage check, and mislabelled traps degrade the teaching payload a student reads after answering. It is minor because the second half of the compound label ("contradicted") is correct and the substantive explanation that follows it is accurate, so the student is not misled about why C is wrong.

findings.claim: Q2 option B is labelled outside_knowledge when the passage in fact contradicts it, which understates the strength of the elimination the rationale offers.
findings.evidence: Option B: "Heat rising from the rooms below kept the space above the boarding warmer than the air outside at night." Rationale: "B = outside_knowledge — a genuinely plausible building-physics claim (warmth from the rooms below) that the passage never makes". But the passage does address night-time state directly: "and by dawn the whole void has given its heat back", i.e. the void does not stay warmer than outside air at night. B is refutable from the text, not merely unsupported by it.
findings.why: Pedagogy review adjudicates whether each distractor's stated misconception is correctly diagnosed. The label is not false — the causal claim genuinely is imported — but the rationale withholds the decisive textual refutation it already quotes elsewhere in the same paragraph, which weakens the teaching value. No verdict-level consequence: B is wrong either way and D remains uniquely keyable.
